source.title: PathProx: A Proximal Gradient Algorithm for Weight Decay Regularized Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Liu Yang; Jifan Zhang; Joseph Shenouda; Dimitris Papailiopoulos; Kangwook Lee; R. Nowak

record.tranche_reason: Compares a proximal weight-decay training method with standard weight-decay training and reports test accuracy on natural and corrupted datasets. It does not test any of the claim's defined versions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports convergence, local Lipschitz constants, decision boundaries and sparsity. Those findings do not measure a version's named behavior; convergence and figure-only findings are not included as rows. Corrupted-data results are out of scope for the claim's in-distribution versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares PathProx with SGD weight decay on accuracy, convergence, robustness and sparsity. None of its experiments tests V1–V8: a proximal optimizer comparison is not an adaptive-optimizer comparison, input Lipschitz constants are not magnitude-aware weight sharpness, and pruning units is not removing memorized training examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that PathProx minimizes the weight-decay objective faster, finds sparse solutions more readily, and can improve generalization and robustness. Accuracy gains vary across tasks.
record.recipe_differences: PathProx applies proximal updates to a path-norm objective equivalent to weight decay; comparisons use SGD with weight decay. Both methods use selected learning rates and weight-decay parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Task, dataset, and true-label versus corrupted-data evaluation condition.

fits_no_version.finding: PathProx has higher mean clean test accuracy in three of four tasks; on full MNIST it scores 98.21% versus 98.29% for weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PathProx can improve held-out accuracy relative to SGD weight decay, with benefits varying by task.

fits_no_version.finding: PathProx improves mean MNIST-C accuracy in both MLP tasks and has slightly lower CIFAR10-C accuracy; the CIFAR10-C difference is smaller than the reported standard errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PathProx's corruption-robustness advantage depends on the task.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports smaller input-Jacobian spectral norms for PathProx on unseen MNIST examples, alongside similar training data loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PathProx can reduce local input sensitivity relative to SGD weight decay.

record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy but not the training-test gap for the Table 1 comparisons. Hyperparameters were selected by validation accuracy; the grid search used one random seed, followed by three additional runs.
record.rows_left_out: Sparsity percentages in Table 1 and Tables 2–3, and sparse-solution comparisons in Figure 5, were omitted because those outcomes do not measure a claim version. Figure-only results from Figures 1–2 were omitted because their outcomes do not directly test the listed versions.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting and held-out chance-accuracy comparison alongside natural-label performance.
No width sweep beyond zero training error; Figure 5 compares selected pruned solutions under explicit regularization.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison on a common image task or test of learned local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison; PathProx is a proximal method.
No batch-size comparison or batch-dependent training-recipe experiment.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No identification or removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. All Table 1 accuracy values and baselines match the supplied text; uncertainties are standard errors over four runs. Missing training-test gaps alone would not disqualify most versions—the required experimental contrasts are absent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance under the same recipe are not compared.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No dropout comparison or joint dropout and weight-decay removal.
Local Lipschitz constants are reported, but the magnitude-aware sharpness measure and training-test gap comparison are not.
